IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.claim: These readers retain the hāʾ in liaison in لم يتسنه and the listed parallel forms; all readers retain it at pause, and all keep it in the two further al-Ḥāqqa forms in both positions.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر هذه الحروف كلها بإثبات الهاء في الوصل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.claim: Ḥamza drops the hāʾ in liaison in all the listed forms; like everyone, he retains it at pause.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī drops the hāʾ in liaison only in لم يتسنه and اقتده, retaining it in the remaining listed forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.anchor: وكان الكسائي يحذف الهاء في الوصل من قوله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r1.claim: Mā can be negative or interrogative; the author prefers the question because it expresses yearning and longing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r1.anchor: I would prefer its latter meaning because in this case it would express yearning and longing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r2.claim: The preposition ʿan after halaka makes the verb carry the sense of going away or disappearing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r2.anchor: shows that the latter encompasses the meaning of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r3.claim: Sulṭān means authority; the speaker longs for the loss of worldly authority that had made him arrogant and heedless of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p455/r3.anchor: They will longingly express the loss of the authority they had in the previous world

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.claim: Most readers retain hāʾ al-sakt in the connected and paused forms for book, reckoning, wealth, and power, and also in mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: كتابيه، وحسابيه في موضعيهما وماليه وسلطانيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin deletes the hāʾ and silences the yāʾ; Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash delete it only in connected speech, while Ḥamza does so for selected forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: بحذفها وصلا ووقفا وإسكان الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.claim: Al-Zuhrawī calls retaining hāʾ in connected speech an error, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because the transmitted reading is mass-transmitted and must be accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.anchor: ليس كما قال، بل ذلك منقول نقل التواتر فوجب قبوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، عكرمة، السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r15.claim: They take سلطانيه to mean his proof or argument used in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r15.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه: أي حجتي، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك وعكرمة والسدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r16.claim: He says worldly kings utter this, meaning their political power has vanished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r16.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يقول ذلك ملوك الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r17.claim: Abd al-Dawla ibn Nuwaih styled himself King of Kings, then failed and went mad, speaking only this verse fragment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r17.anchor: وكان عضد الدولة ابن نويه لما تسمى بملك الأملاك غلاب القدر لم يفلح وجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r3.claim: He rejects the exclusivity inferred from fronting as neither Sibawayh's nor expert grammarians' doctrine, and calls Ibn Zayd's kingly-status explanation weak; Ibn Abbas's proof-reading fits all the damned, not kings alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r3.anchor: وإنما قدره لا تصلوه إلا الجحيم، لأنه يزعم أن تقديم المفعول يدل على الحصر

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says his lost sulṭān was the argument he had used against Muhammad in worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ضلت عني حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها على محمد في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r4.claim: Muqātil says his argument was lost when his bodily limbs testified to his associating partners with God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : ضلت عني حجتي يعني حين شهدت عليه الجوارح بالشرك

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r5.claim: Another view is that his rule and control over people have vanished, leaving him poor and abased.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r5.anchor: الثاني : ذهب ملكي وتسلطي على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r6.claim: A further explanation is that he disputed with the truthful only because of his kingship; now the power is gone and only its penalty remains.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r6.anchor: قيل معناه : إنني إنما كنت أنازع المحقين بسبب الملك والسلطان ، فالآن ذهب ذلك الملك وبقي الوبال

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.claim: The blessed were first described in joy and good living, eating and drinking; correspondingly the wretched are introduced through grief before their restraints and food.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى ذكر سرور السعداء أولا ، ثم ذكر أحوالهم في العيش الطيب وفي الأكل والشرب ، كذا ههنا

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r23.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r23.claim: Sulṭāniyah means authority or warrant; its passing means the person no longer controls his destiny and regrets neglecting preparation for the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r23.anchor: My power translates sulṭāniyah, which indicates authority and warrant; that it has passed means that those who receive the book in their left hand no longer have any control over their own destiny

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r24.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r24.claim: Sulṭān can also mean argument or proof (ḥujjah).
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r24.anchor: Here and in other verses, sulṭān also connotes “argument” or “proof” (ḥujjah; Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r25.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r25.claim: The person can no longer argue against the Resurrection or defend himself because his limbs testify to his life and he must admit his sin.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r25.anchor: they no longer have any capacity to argue against the reality of the Resurrection or even to argue for themselves

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r2.claim: The speaker says his proofs and arguments have vanished, leaving him no case to present.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r2.anchor: يقول: ذهبت عني حججي، وضلت، فلا حجة لي أحتج بها

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every proof vanished and could avail the speaker nothing.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] يقول: ضلت عني كل بينة فلم تغن عني شيئا

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r4.claim: ʿIkrima glosses sulṭāniya as my proof or argument.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r4.anchor: عن النضر بن عربي، قال: سمعت عكرمة، يقول: {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] قال: حجتي

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r5.claim: Mujāhid likewise glosses sulṭāniya as my proof or argument.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] قال: حجتي

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r6.claim: Qatāda says not everyone entering Hell was a village ruler who collected revenues; God gave people power over their peers and commanded obedience while forbidding disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] أما والله ما كل من دخل النار كان أمير قرية يجبيها

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses sulṭāniya as my proof, which has gone astray.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r7.anchor: قال: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول: أخبرنا عبيد، قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] يقول: بينتي ضلت عني

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says sulṭān here means worldly dominion.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} [الحاقة: 29] قال: سلطان الدنيا

TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.claim: These are words of regret: he had treated wealth and power as keys to happiness, protection from harm, and control of what he desired, and had labored for them while turning from God and truth.
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.anchor: كلمتا تحسر يقولهما حيث يرى خيبة سعيه في الدنيا فإنه كان يحسب أن مفتاح سعادته في الحياة

TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.claim: Seeing that worldly means have collapsed and wealth and children cannot help on this Day, he laments his wealth’s uselessness and his power’s failure; regret now avails nothing.
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.anchor: فلما شاهد تقطع الأسباب وأنه في يوم لا ينفع فيه مال ولا بنون ذكر عدم نفع ما له وبطلان سلطانه

BURSEVI:v10p110/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p110/r6.claim: Al-Raghib derives sultan from mastery by force; it can denote power, its possessor, or an argument, whose force reaches hearts, especially those of learned believers.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r6.anchor: قال الراغب السلاطة التمكن من القهر ومنه سمى السلطان والسلطان يقال في السلاطة

BURSEVI:v10p110/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r7.claim: One reading is that his kingship and control over people have vanished, leaving him poor and humiliated.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r7.anchor: ملكي وتسلطي على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

BURSEVI:v10p110/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p110/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the lost sultan as the argument the speaker used to make against others in worldly life, now rendered void.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r8.anchor: كما روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ومعناه بطلت هجتي التي كنت أحتج بها عليهم في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p110/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r9.claim: The argument reading is more fitting because receiving the record in the left hand applies to all the wretched, not only kings.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r9.anchor: ورجح هذا المعنى بأن من أوتى كتابه بشماله لا اختصاص له بالملوك بل هو عام لجميع أهل الشقاوة

BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.claim: The wealth wording alludes to wealthy Quraysh leaders such as al-Walid, while the mention of lost power exposes their worldly status.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.anchor: يدل على الأول على أن فيه تعريضا بنحو الوليد من رؤساء قريش وأهل ثروتهم

BURSEVI:v10p110/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r11.claim: Lost sultan may also mean losing command over one's powers, faculties, and limbs, which one can no longer employ in worship at resurrection.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المنى تسلطي على القوى والآلات فعجزت عن استمالها في العبادات

THALABI:v10p30/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p30/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p30/r12.claim: Most commentators take the lines to mean that his wealth did not help and his proof or argument has vanished.
THALABI:v10p30/r12.anchor: ذهبت عني حجتي عن أكثر المفسرين،

THALABI:v10p30/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p30/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p30/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets it as the loss of his kingdom, authority, and command.
THALABI:v10p30/r13.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: زال عني ملكي وقولي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r1.claim: ʿAta, reporting from Ibn Abbas, says the speaker means that his argument against Muhammad has escaped him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r1.anchor: ضلت عني حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها على محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r2.claim: Muqatil says his argument failed when his limbs testified against him for associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ضلت عني حجتي، يعني: حين شهدت عليه الجوارح بالشرك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r3.speaker: الربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ understands it as the authority he possessed in worldly life and says he was obeyed by his companions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd similarly says that his sovereignty has vanished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال ابن زيد: زال عني ملكي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r5.claim: Most commentators, including Mujahid and al-Dahhak, take sulṭān to mean proof or argument.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says every person has authority over his own self, religion, and livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: قد جعل لكل إنسان سلطانا على نفسه ودينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r7.claim: On al-Hasan’s view, the phrase means that his dominion is gone and he has no control over himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r8.claim: He regrets and understands only when regret can no longer help; had this happened in worldly life while his power remained, it would have benefited him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r8.anchor: وذلك أنه ندم وعلم حين لم ينفعه ذلك، ولو كان ذلك في

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:29-32/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:29-32/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:29-32/r1.claim: His proof has vanished, and his dominion and power are gone.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:29-32/r1.anchor: { هلك عني سلطانيه } ذهب عني حجتي، وزال عني ملكي وقوتي، فيقول الله لخزنة جهنم.

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r23.claim: Sultān may mean the sovereignty, property, government, and wealth he boasted in and relied on, or all the proofs and arguments he clung to; he is left helpless.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r23.anchor: onunla iftihar ettiğim, herkese tasallut ettiğim

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r24.claim: This regret fits rulers and wealthy holders of power who trusted worldly dominion, punished others, but denied punishment in their own case and committed injustice.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r24.anchor: Böyle bir sözle nedâmet ve tahassür belli ki dünya saltanatına güvenip

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r25.speaker: Müfessirler
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r25.claim: Commentators report that Adud al-Dawla (Fannā Khusraw b. Buwayh) wrote verses celebrating wine, singers, and a drinking gathering.

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r1.claim: The poem's closing line styles its author as Adud al-Dawla, king of kings, and vanquisher of fate.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r1.anchor: عــضــد الدولة وابــن ركنـهـا مــلك الأمــلاك غــلاب القــدر

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.claim: Soon after boasting of conquering fate, Fannā Khusraw went mad and died repeating that his wealth and authority had failed him.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.anchor: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ diye diye can verip gitmişti.

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r3.claim: The author leaves whether death ended the matter to God; the ruler who styled himself fate's conqueror was himself crushed by fate.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r3.anchor: Şimdi görülmüş bir şey varsa bu sözü defterine

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.claim: The final hā in kitābiyeh, hisābiyeh, māliyeh, and sultāniyeh is hāʾ al-sakt, used at pause after fatḥa and always read with sukūn; the underlying forms end in -iya.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.anchor: “Kitâbiyeh, hisâbiyeh, mâliyeh, sultâniyeh” fâsılalarında ها fetha üzerine vakf için hâ-i sekittir. Dâima sâkin okunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.claim: Wealth, property, sovereignty, status, and power all disappear; only a person's good or bad beliefs and deeds remain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.anchor: mal, mülk, saltanat, makam, güç vb. dünyaya ait ne varsa hepsi yok olup gitmiş, sadece insanın olumlu veya olumsuz inanç ve amelleri kalmıştır

BURHAN:v1p343/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p343/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p343/r5.claim: For Qur'anic words written with pause hāʾ, stop on the hāʾ: connecting would require deleting it under Arabic grammar, while retaining it in connection would oppose that grammar; stopping honors both grammar and the codex.
BURHAN:v1p343/r5.anchor: فالواجب أن يوقف عليه بالهاء لأنه مكتوب في المصحف بالهاء ولا يوصل لأنه يلزم في حكم العربية إسقاط الهاء في الوصل

BURHAN:v1p343/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p343/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p343/r6.claim: Reported connection of these hāʾ endings is actually recitation with the intention of pausing, with only a brief interval between sounds.
BURHAN:v1p343/r6.anchor: أتو به على نية الوقف غير أنهم قصروا زمن الفصل بين النطقين فظن من لا خيرة له أنهم وصلوا وصلا محضا وليس كذلك

BURHAN:v4p430/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.claim: Hāʾ al-sakt marks a pause and follows a built ending to preserve its vowel; it is normally deleted in connected speech, while the codex spellings support stopping on it.
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.anchor: وتلحق وقفا لبيان الحركة وإنما تلحق بحركة بناء لا تشبه حركة الإعراب

BURHAN:v4p430/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.speaker: حمزة
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.claim: The readers retain hāʾ in connection in كتابيه and حسابيه on pausal intent; Hamza deletes it in three other words when connecting but retains it at a stop.

BURHAN:v3p340/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p340/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p340/r15.claim: هلك here means that my authority has vanished.

ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.claim: A pause hāʾ is appended to forms such as māliyah and sulṭāniyah; readers also pronounce it at the pauses on plural verse endings.
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.anchor: وحرف للغيبة وهو اللاحق لإيا وللسكت نحو ﴿ ما هيه ﴾ ﴿ كتابيه ﴾ ﴿ حسابيه ﴾ ﴿ سلطانيه ﴾ ﴿ ماليه ﴾

ITQAN:v3p269/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.claim: The pause hāʾ is used at verse endings in māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and mā hiyah.
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.anchor: إثبات هاء السكت نحو ﴿ ماليه ﴾ ﴿ سلطانيه ﴾ ﴿ ما هيه ﴾

TUSTARI:69:29/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:29/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:69:29/r1.claim: His lost authority means his argument and excuse.

KHATTABI:v1p37/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p37/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p37/r5.claim: An objection says halāk is used for concrete people and things, not abstractions such as authority or knowledge.
KHATTABI:v1p37/r5.anchor: وكقوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} وإنما يستعمل لفظ الهلاك في الأعيان والأشخاص

KHATTABI:v1p44/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r1.claim: The fragment cites an Arabic idiom in which a man ‘walks’ when he has many children; the line about a sheep not walking on the wolf means it does not reproduce abundantly.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r1.anchor: مشى الرجل إذا كثر ولده. وأنشدوا:

KHATTABI:v1p44/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r2.claim: Metaphor can be stronger than literal wording: ‘strip’ for the night’s removal of day and ‘proclaim’ for openly carrying out a command are more forceful than literal alternatives.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r2.anchor: والسلخ ها هنا مستعار وهو أبلغ منه لو قال نخرج من النهار

KHATTABI:v1p44/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r3.claim: Calling authority destroyed is stronger than saying it went away, since something that merely departs may return, while destruction leaves no remnant or reversal.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الذهاب قد يكون على مراصدة العود , وليس مع الهلاك بقيا ولا رجعى

KHATTABI:v1p44/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r4.speaker: قيل
KHATTABI:v1p44/r4.claim: An alternative interpretation takes sulṭāniya here to mean proof and argument.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r4.anchor: وقد قيل إن معنى السلطان ها هنا الحجة والبرهان

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r3.claim: Halaka can mean to be lost or to disappear; the speaker's proof has vanished.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r3.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه أي ضل عني حجتي

DAMGHANI:v1p242/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r3.claim: Sulṭān can mean proof or argument; the source says this is the meaning in all Qurʾānic mentions concerning Moses.
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r3.anchor: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

NAHHAS:v5p21/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p21/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p21/r19.claim: The hāʾ is treated as in حسابيه.

ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n15/r1.speaker: Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n15/r1.claim: These exegetes, quoted by Tabari, take sultan as argument or hujjah; Asad adopts this sense for arguments against life after death and divine judgment, though the word primarily means power or authority.
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n15/r1.anchor: meaning of "argument", synonymous with hujjah (Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, all of them quoted by Tabari)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.claim: The hāʾ endings in the Resurrection scene convey exhaustion, hardship, and pain; the author relates the sound to sighing and the long, severe wait for intercession.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.anchor: إذن استخدام حرف الهاء في فواصل هذه السورة يدل على التعب والعناء والألم والهاء مأخوذة من الآه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.claim: The hāʾ endings in the judgment-day words evoke the exhausted people’s sigh, hardship, and pain during the long ordeal; the sound choice reflects the scene’s psychological weight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.anchor: إذن استخدام حرف الهاء في فواصل هذه السورة يدل على التعب والعناء والألم والهاء مأخوذة من الآه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.claim: Kufr is broader than denial: Al Imran 3:10 names wealth and children, while other verses show followers, authority, gods, and intercessors cannot help; a particular instance of disbelief is therefore called denial.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.anchor: نلاحظ قلنا أن الكفر أعمّ من التكذيب، ننظر في الآيات: ذكر في آل عمران حالة جزئية

NASHR:v2p21/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r1.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v2p21/r1.claim: Makki argues that anyone using naql in “كتابيَهْ إني” should assimilate the hāʾ in “ماليه هلك,” since naql treats it as original; he nevertheless says he read with izhar and considers it the correct practice.
NASHR:v2p21/r1.anchor: وقال مكي في تبصرته: يلزم من ألقى الحركة في كتابيه إني أن يدغم ماليه هلك

NASHR:v2p21/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v2p21/r2.claim: Abu Shama says izhar here requires a slight pause; if the reader truly connects, the sound must either assimilate or be vocalized, and omitting both amounts to an unrecognized pause.
NASHR:v2p21/r2.anchor: قال أبو شامة يعني بالإظهار أن يقف على ماليه هلك وقفة لطيفة

NASHR:v2p21/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن السخاوي
NASHR:v2p21/r3.claim: Al-Sakhawi prefers stopping because the hāʾ was added for pause; if connected, he prefers izhar since the hāʾ remains intended as paused and the following hāʾ is separate.
NASHR:v2p21/r3.anchor: والمختار فيه أن يوقف عليه؛ لأن الهاء إنما اجتلبت للوقف فلا يجوز أن توصل

NASHR:v2p21/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p21/r4.claim: The author finds Abu Shama’s explanation most precise and follows al-Dani: with tahqiq, make a light pause on hāʾ while notionally connecting; with ilqa, connect and assimilate because hāʾ is treated as original.
NASHR:v2p21/r4.anchor: وما قاله أبو شامة أقرب إلى التحقيق، وأحرى بالدراية والتدقيق

NASHR:v2p142/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p142/r7.speaker: حمزة، ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p142/r7.claim: Hamza and Yaʿqūb omit the hāʾ of māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and māhiyah in connection; the others retain it in both positions.
NASHR:v2p142/r7.anchor: فحذف الهاء من الثلاثة في الوصل حمزة ويعقوب

QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#1/r1.speaker: Cs
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#1/r1.claim: Cs deletes the hāʾ al-sakta from māliyah and connects it to halaka without pause, making māliyah flow syntactically into the verb instead of standing as an independent exclamation.
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#1/r1.anchor: Cs, mutawatir: Deletion of hāʾ al-sakta on māliyah, connecting the two words without pause

QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#2/r1.speaker: Assim
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#2/r1.claim: Assim assimilates the hāʾ al-sakta into the initial hāʾ of halaka; the pause marker merges with the verb onset and produces a geminated consonant.
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:1#2/r1.anchor: Assim, mutawatir: Assimilation of hāʾ al-sakta into the hāʾ of halaka

QIRAAT-ER:69:29:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:3#1/r1.speaker: Cs
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:3#1/r1.claim: Cs retains hāʾ al-sakta in pausal recitation but drops it in connected recitation, giving a canonical variation in the word ending.
QIRAAT-ER:69:29:3#1/r1.anchor: Cs, mutawatir: Hāʾ al-sakta present in pause, dropped in continuous recitation

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك وعكرمة والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿIkrima, al-Suddī, and most early authorities understand sulṭāniya as the argument he used in worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r1.anchor: وبه فسره ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك وعكرمة والسدي وأكثر السلف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r2.claim: Another view takes it as kingship and power over people, now lost, leaving him poor and humiliated.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r2.anchor: أو ملكي وتسلطي على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r3.claim: Qatāda takes it as control over bodily powers and faculties, which he failed to use in obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r3.anchor: أو تسلطي على القوى والآلات التي خلقت لي فعجزت عن استعمالها في الطاعات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r4.claim: Qatāda says those entering Hell were not all town rulers: God gave them control of their bodies and commanded obedience while forbidding disobedience; Al-Ālūsī uses this to weigh the interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r4.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد عنه أنه قال أما والله ما كل من دخل النار كان أمير قرية ولكن الله تعالى خلقهم وسلطهم على أبدانهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors the argument meaning over kingship, while noting the following words may suit the kingship reading better.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r5.anchor: وبما أشار إليه رجح الأول على الثاني أيضا لكن قيل ما بعد أشد مناسبة له

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأسد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r7.speaker: الثعالبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r7.claim: A story says the Buyid ruler ʿAḍud al-Dawla (Fannā Khusraw), after reciting a poem, later went mad and could utter only this verse; al-Thaʿālibī says he could recite only it at death.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r7.anchor: ويحكى عنه فناخسرة المقلب بعضد الدولة ابن بويه أنه لما أنشد قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported to assimilate the pause hāʾ of māliya into the hāʾ of halaka; Al-Ālūsī calls this weak because pause hāʾ is necessarily distinct.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r8.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو أنه أدغم هاء السكت من ماليه في هاء هلك وهو ضعيف قياسا لأن هاء السكت لا تدغم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r9.speaker: ورش
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r9.claim: Although assimilation is attributed to Warsh, the correction says what is transmitted from him is naql in kitābiyya, not this assimilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#3/r9.anchor: وفيه رواية الإدغام فيما ذكر عن ورش وعقب بأن المروي عنه إنما هو النقل في كتابيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r9.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r9.claim: Most commentators say his proof or argument has vanished from him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r9.anchor: {هلك عني سلطانيه} ضلت عني حجتي، عن أكثر المفسرين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the loss as the disappearance of his rule and strength.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r10.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: زال عني ملكي وقوتي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r7.claim: Sulṭānihi may mean his rule and power over people or the argument he used in worldly life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r7.anchor: ملكي وتسلطي على الناس، أو حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها في الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.speaker: حمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.claim: Ḥamza drops both final hāʾs in connected reading; the other readers retain them in both connected and paused forms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «عني» «مالي» «عني سلطاني» بحذف الهاءين في الوصل والباقون بإثباتها في الحالين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r1.claim: Wealth had been a means to attain authority, but it has failed to secure that authority or help him now.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r1.anchor: قال نافيا لما أوصله إليه ماله شارحا لعدم إغنائه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r2.claim: “Sulṭān” includes his domination of callers to God through specious arguments, which his tongue and its helpers advanced despite their evident falsity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r2.anchor: تسلطي على الدعاة إلى الله بالشبه الباطلة التي كان يطلب اللسان بها فأساعده عليها مع ظهور بطلانها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r3.claim: His worldly kingship, obtained through wealth, has vanished, and those who supported him are now even farther away.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r3.anchor: الملك الذي أوصل إليه المال فعاد لأن ذلك الملك الأعظم هلك والمساعد أبعد مباعد

DURR-FULL:v8p273/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r4.claim: Qatada says they wished death; on vanished authority, he says not everyone entering Hell was a village ruler, since God gave people control of their bodies and commanded obedience while forbidding disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {يا ليتها كانت القاضية} قال: تمنوا الموت ولم يكن شيء في الدنيا أكره عندهم من الموت وفي قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه}

DURR-FULL:v8p273/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets sulṭāniya as my argument or proof.
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد {هلك عني سلطانيه} قال: حجتي

DURR-FULL:v8p273/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r6.claim: Ikrima likewise glosses sulṭāniya as my argument or proof.
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة {هلك عني سلطانيه} قال: يعني حجته

DURR-FULL:v8p273/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says every proof deserted him and gained him nothing.
DURR-FULL:v8p273/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {هلك عني سلطانيه} قال: ضلت عني كل بينة فلم تغن عني شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r6.claim: The authority’s “perishing” is metaphorical: it no longer benefits or accompanies him on that day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r6.anchor: ومعنى هلاك السلطان : عدم الانتفاع به يومئذ فهو هلاك مجازي .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r7.claim: Halaka is construed with ʿan because it also implies absence: his former power is no longer present.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r7.anchor: وضمن { هلك } معنى ( غاب ) فعدي ب ( عن ) ، أي لم يحضرني سلطاني الذي عهدته .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.speaker: حمزة وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.claim: Ḥamza and Khalaf omit the hāʾ of māliya and sulṭāniya in connected recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.anchor: إلا أن حمزة وخلفا قرآ هنا { ما أغنى عني ماليه هلك عني سلطانيه } بدون هاء في حالة الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r1.claim: The fragment refers to an interpretation of السلطان as proof or argument, attributed to ʿIkrima and Mujahid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r2.claim: A view favored by Ibn Zayd takes the word as the worldly rule or authority voiced by unbelieving kings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم ونحا إليه ابن زيد ينطق بذلك ملوك الدنيا الكفرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers that each person’s sultan is his worldly condition, including his numbers and resources.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r3.anchor: والظاهرة عندي أن سلطان كل أحد حاله في الدنيا من عدد وعدد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r4.claim: The Prophet’s rule that a man must not be led in his domain or seated in his place without permission illustrates the use of sultan for one’s authority or standing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p360#2/r4.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يؤمن الرجل في سلطانه ولا يجلس على تكرمته إلا بإذنه»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r1.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، الضحاك، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r1.claim: His authority here is his proof or argument, which has vanished from him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r1.anchor: أحدهما ضلت عني حجتي قاله مجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r2.claim: An alternative meaning is that his sovereignty has departed from him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353/r2.anchor: والثاني زال عني ملكي قاله ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.claim: Neither wealth nor worldly standing protected him from God's punishment; he is left alone without helper or rescuer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.anchor: أي: لم يدفع عني مالي ولا جاهي عذاب الله وبأسه، بل خلص الأمر إلي وحدي، فلا معين لي ولا مجير.

JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.claim: Hamza and Yaqub drop the final h in connection for māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿa; all retain it at pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب: ماليه وسلطانيه وفي سورة (القارعة) (ما هيه) بحذف الهاء في الوصل،

JISHUMI:v2p1011/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1011/r3.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v2p1011/r3.claim: Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb omit the hāʾ of سلطانيه in connected recitation; the other readers retain it.
JISHUMI:v2p1011/r3.anchor: وعن حمزة ويعقوب في سورة الحاقة سلطانيه وفي القارعة: ما هيه بحذف الهاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r4.claim: سلطانيه means his power and domination over people; now he is left poor and humiliated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r4.anchor: ملكي وتسلطى على الناس ، وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : أنها نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأشد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r6.claim: Fanakhusra, called al-Adud, boasted in a poem of his power, then went mad and could speak only this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r6.anchor: وعن فناخسرة الملقب بالعضد ، أنه لما قال : عضد الدولة وابن ركنها … ملك الأملاك غلاب القدر لم يفلح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the loss of authority as the failure of the argument he used in worldly life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : ضلت عني حجتي . ومعناه : بطلت حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها في الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r9.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r9.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak explain his lost authority as losing his argument.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r9.anchor: معناه ضللت عن حجتي , قاله مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي والضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r10.claim: Qatada takes the lost authority to be the power he used over his own body to commit sin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r10.anchor: سلطانه الذي تسلط به على بدنه حتى أقدم به على معصيته , وهذا معنى قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r11.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r11.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says that in worldly life he commanded followers and was secure in his invulnerability.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r11.anchor: أنه كان في الدنيا مطاعا في أتباعه , عزيزا في امتناعه , وهذا معنى قول الربيع بن أنس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r12.claim: A report identifies the passage with Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r12.anchor: وحكي أن هذا في أبي جهل بن هشام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r13.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak says it was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r13.anchor: وذكر الضحاك أنها نزلت في الأسود ابن عبد الأسد

MUQATIL:69:25-32/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r5.claim: His argument has vanished, and his bodily limbs testified against him for associating partners with God.
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r5.anchor: يقول: ضلت عني يومئد حجتي شهدت عليه الجوارح بالشرك، يقول الله لخزنة جهنم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r1.claim: “My authority” means his kingship and power over people; he is left poor and humiliated.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r1.anchor: ملكى وتسلطى على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the word means his proof: the argument he used in worldly life has failed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#5/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ضلت عنى حجتى أى بطلت حجتى التى كنت احتج بها فى الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، السدي، الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak explain that his proof or argument has vanished.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r2.anchor: } تفسير ابن عباس: هلكت عني حجتي. وهو قول مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي والضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes his lost authority as his worldly kingship; the man had been obeyed by his companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يعني سلطانيه في الدنيا الذي هو الملك. وكان هذا الرجل مطاعا في أصحابه
